annotation.title_clean: Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
annotation.title_en: Law No. (4) of 2020 Regulating Unmanned Aircraft in the Emirate of Dubai
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ruler of Dubai (Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum); Supreme Legislation Committee in the Emirate of Dubai
annotation.venue: Dubai Official Gazette / Supreme Legislation Committee
annotation.summary_en: Dubai Law No. 4 of 2020 regulates all civilian unmanned aircraft (radio-controlled, remotely piloted, autonomous) in the Emirate. It sets up DCAA permitting, registration, operator and pilot qualification, airspace zoning, privacy protections, mandatory third-party insurance, penalties and liability for damage. Military drones are excluded.
key_provisions_or_claims: Permits from the DCAA required to operate, design, manufacture, import, sell or train on unmanned aircraft.
All unmanned aircraft must be registered and display identification; DCAA keeps a register.
Operators must hold third-party liability insurance and an Operational Safety Certificate, and report accidents and incidents.
Airspace divided into approved, prohibited, restricted and danger areas; operations only in approved areas.
Privacy protections, bans on hacking or seizing drones, imprisonment or fines, and compensation liability for damage.
